A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 24-page Syn2Seq-Forcing paper, including complete supplementary material. Text and rendered pages support a reliable comparison; differences are confined to first-page author information and version metadata.

before.justification: v1 reports original Exo2Ego generation experiments on Ego-Exo4D, including quantitative comparisons in Table 2, ablations in Tables 3–5, and qualitative results in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original quantitative experiments, ablations, and qualitative generation results in the main text and supplement.

M1.justification: The WFLF interpolation, pose interpolation, DFoT-based sequential model, training objective, and inference procedure are identical in both versions.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training coverage and evaluate Exo2Ego generation on the Bike, Health, and Cooking categories of Ego-Exo4D. No dataset, task, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains Trj-Crafter, Wan-FCtrl, Wan VACE, and Exo2EgoSyn. Comparator membership in the interpolation and pose-embedding experiments is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The data splits, video counts, 256×256 resolution, nine-frame sampling, training budgets, and PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS evaluation remain identical, including supplementary settings.

E4.justification: Tables 3–5 retain the same frame/pose interpolation, interpolator-choice, and pose-embedding ablations. Main-text and supplementary qualitative examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative results are identical. For example, Table 2 reports the same Health results for the proposed method: PSNR 16.7139, SSIM 0.5728, and LPIPS 0.4828.

T1.justification: The task formulation, loss, and interpolation equations in Section 3 are unchanged, as are the supplementary SLERP definitions and numerical-stability treatment.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain identical claims about synchronization-induced discontinuities, interpolation-based sequential modeling, and potential bidirectional generation.

C2.justification: Interpretations of interpolation gains and pose embeddings are unchanged. The supplementary Future Work discussion retains the same qualifications about pose assumptions, computational costs, and limited fine-tuning data.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information is identical, including WFLF prompts, preprocessing, U-ViT3D conditioning, AdamW settings, H200 hardware, training times, and inference guidance.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, positioning against earlier approaches, and all 54 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: On page 1, the corresponding-author marker moves from Danda Pani Paudel to Mohammad Mahdi, and the arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 15 April to v2 dated 26 June 2026. The supplementary title page still marks Paudel; all scientific prose and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Moving the corresponding-author marker slightly changes first-page author spacing, and the updated margin stamp shifts slightly. All figures, tables, captions, and rendered pages 2–24 are identical.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, and reproducibility information are identical. The first-page updates introduce a small inconsistency with the supplementary corresponding-author marker, but these administrative edits do not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
